extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, experimental scientists, and methodologists interested in empirical induction
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural method for discovering forms, latent processes, and latent conformation in nature by systematic collection of instances, negative instances, degrees, and carefully designed experiments followed by legitimate induction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two kinds of axioms: simple natures and latent processes/conformation
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish axioms that regard simple natures (primary, universal, eternal forms) from those that depend on the discovery of latent processes or conformation in concrete bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary axioms (simple natures/forms) are the basis for higher and radical operations on nature; latent-process/conformation axioms arise from concrete bodies and their usual courses (e.g., generation of metals, plants, animals). Both kinds are necessary but primary axioms govern the deepest causes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of inquiry: metaphysics (forms) vs physics (efficient causes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let investigation of forms (eternal and immutable in reasoning) constitute metaphysics; investigation of the efficient cause of matter, latent process, and latent conformation constitute physics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parallel practical divisions: mechanics corresponding to physics, and (in Bacon's usage) magic corresponding to metaphysics as practical command over nature. Choose the appropriate division for the question under study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare a complete and accurate natural and experimental history
rubrics_metrics.description: First prepare, as a foundation for the whole, a complete and accurate natural and experimental history — 'We must not imagine or invent, but discover the acts and properties of nature.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because natural history is varied and diffuse it must be fixed and exhibited in due order by forming tables and co-ordinations so the understanding can act upon them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three ministrations for eliciting axioms: to the senses, memory, and mind/reason
rubrics_metrics.description: The process of eliciting axioms from experiment admits of three ministrations: 1) to the senses, 2) to the memory, 3) to the mind or reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect sensory data, organize and retain it (memory/tables), then apply reasonive induction. Bacon instructs: 'Our third ministration, therefore, must be true and legitimate induction, the very key of interpretation. We must begin, however, at the end, and go back again to the others.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Table of existence / presence (instances agreeing in the form)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exhibit to the understanding all known instances which agree in the same nature (a table of existence/presence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect many diverse instances where the queried nature is manifest (Bacon's long enumerated list for heat: sun rays, burning mirrors, flame, warm baths, friction, certain chemicals, animal heat, etc.) — use such tables as raw data for induction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table of deviation / absence in proximity (negative instances)
rubrics_metrics.description: Present instances which do not admit of the given nature, focusing especially on objects closely connected to those in which the nature is present (a table of deviation or absence in proximity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Negatives must be classed under the affirmatives. Do not try to examine every instance; choose proximate negatives that are closely related to positives to make the labor finite and informative (e.g., lunar rays vs solar rays, mountain summits, polar reflections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Table of degrees / comparative instances
rubrics_metrics.description: Exhibit instances in which the nature is present in greater or less degree, by comparing increase and decrease in the same object or degree in different objects (table of degrees/comparative instances).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A true form should vary uniformly with the given nature; use comparative degrees to identify essence (e.g., comparative warmth across animals, parts of animals, materials, confined vs unconfined substances).

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect instances as plain history without premature reflection
rubrics_metrics.description: When gathering instances for form-investigation, collection must be made as a mere history and without any premature reflection or too great refinement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid early theorizing; first amass observations neutrally so the subsequent inductive work is not biased by prior hypothesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: True and legitimate induction (begin at the end; iterative elimination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply true and legitimate induction to derive axioms from the tables — 'the very key of interpretation' — starting at the end and iteratively returning to senses and memory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the three tables (presence, absence, degrees) together to exclude non-essential circumstances and isolate the form; proceed by methodical exclusions and eliminations rather than conjectural leaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design targeted experiments to resolve specific questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Deduce new experiments from axioms and design experiments tailored to test particular uncertainties or hypotheses (e.g., lens/burning-glass tests, thermometric trials, confined-air jars).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bacon gives concrete experimental prescriptions: test whether lunar rays can be concentrated to produce heat (use thermometer), try burning-glass on warm non-luminous objects, enclose air in earthen jars to test intrinsic heat, try spirits of wine in covered cavities, etc. Experiments should be controlled and devised to illuminate the specific doubtful point raised by the tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate latent processes by tracing minute, often imperceptible efforts
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek the continued processes and smallest efforts that escape ordinary senses in generations and transformations — ask what is lost, what remains, what is added, what is diluted, what predominates, what impedes, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Latent processes often involve tiny forces or gradual steps; careful, sensitive observation and experiment are required to perceive and record them, since direct sensory detection may fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate latent conformation by reasoning and induction rather than destructive separation
rubrics_metrics.description: To discover the real conformation (texture, spirit, tangible essence, pores) of compounds, prefer reasoning and true induction with experiment and comparison rather than separation by fire, which often superinduces altered natures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While distillation and separation can reveal component differences, they frequently create new natures by heat; prefer comparative induction and non-destructive methods to infer internal conformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use organized tables and coordinations so the understanding may act upon observations
rubrics_metrics.description: Fix and exhibit the varied and diffuse natural history in due order by forming tables and co-ordinations of instances so the understanding can operate on them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Well-ordered records reduce confusion and distraction and enable systematic inductive work; structure observations into the three tables and further classificatory schemes as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply mathematics and quantitative reasoning to physical inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct inquiry to simple natures and apply mathematics to physics; transfer attention from the complicated to the simple and from the indefinite to the definite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not be alarmed by fractions or large numbers — use calculation freely (e.g., treat thousandths as readily as units). Quantification clarifies relations and renders phenomena commensurable for induction.
